item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is inviting young people from around the world to connect through the Global Youth Network for Human Rights and contribute their perspectives on human rights in their communities.

Coordinated by OHCHR through its Child and Youth Rights Unit, the Network provides an inclusive space for young people from diverse backgrounds to engage with human rights issues, exchange perspectives, and learn about opportunities to participate in the work of OHCHR and its partners. Young people do not need to belong to a formal organization or have previous human rights experience to join.

Alongside the Network, young people are invited to complete a survey on Youth Perspectives on Human Rights Cities. The survey is being organized by the UN Human Rights Office, United Cities and Local Governments (UCLG), and SDSN Youth. Responses will help inform a session titled “Human Rights Cities: From Awareness to Local Action” at the UN Youth Townhall in Heidelberg, Germany, taking place from 8 to 10 December 2026.

About the Global Youth Network for Human Rights

The Global Youth Network for Human Rights aims to strengthen ongoing dialogue and collaboration between OHCHR and young people across regions. It builds on young people’s interest in OHCHR’s youth engagement initiatives and seeks to include those who may not have access to established youth participation platforms.

Through the Network, participants can share their views, contribute to human rights discussions, and stay informed about opportunities to engage with OHCHR and its partners. The initiative is designed to connect a diverse global community and help ensure that young people’s perspectives meaningfully inform human rights work.

What Does the Network Do?

The Network serves as a platform for youth engagement in several ways:

  • Gathering youth perspectives: Young people may be invited to share their views through surveys, consultations, and calls for input.
  • Sharing information and resources: Participants can receive information about human rights resources and opportunities for youth engagement.
  • Mobilizing youth participation: The Network may invite young people to contribute to campaigns and consultations, including initiatives such as the Global Alliance for Human Rights.
  • Supporting youth-led action: It encourages young people to take action within their own communities and contribute to local human rights efforts.

These activities enable OHCHR to engage with young people from different regions and backgrounds, including those who are not affiliated with formal organizations.

Who Can Join the Network?

The Global Youth Network for Human Rights is open to all young people interested in human rights, regardless of their:

  • Background or identity
  • Existing knowledge of human rights
  • Previous experience
  • Organizational or institutional affiliation

The Network particularly aims to reach young people who may not have access to traditional youth participation opportunities. The information provided does not specify a particular nationality, country, continent, educational qualification, or professional background as a requirement for joining.

How Does the Network Work?

The Network operates primarily through email communication, allowing OHCHR to connect with thousands of young people around the world.

Participants may:

  • Receive periodic updates and invitations to engage.
  • Contribute to surveys and consultations.
  • Participate in campaigns and awareness-raising activities.

Participation is flexible and does not require a fixed time commitment. Joining the Network provides a way to stay informed and consider opportunities to contribute when they arise.

Youth Perspectives on Human Rights Cities: Survey Details

The UN Human Rights Office, UCLG, and SDSN Youth are collecting youth perspectives for a session on Human Rights Cities at the UN Youth Townhall in Heidelberg, Germany, from 8 to 10 December 2026.

The survey invites young people to reflect on their experiences in their cities or municipalities and explain what a “Human Rights City” means to them. Responses will help shape the session discussion and identify youth recommendations for more rights-based local governance.

What Is the Survey About?

The survey asks participants to consider how human rights are respected, protected, and fulfilled in their local communities. It explores both areas where progress is being made and challenges that remain.

Participants are asked about:

  • Their country and, optionally, the city or municipality they are discussing.
  • Their age group and gender.
  • Their familiarity with the concept of a Human Rights City.
  • Whether their municipality has joined or committed to the Human Rights Cities movement, if they know.
  • Areas where rights are being respected in practice, such as access to essential services, equality and freedom from discrimination, youth participation, transparency, accountability, and a safe, clean, and healthy environment.
  • Examples of local policies, services, initiatives, or community practices that support human rights.
  • Gaps and challenges affecting the protection and fulfilment of rights.
  • Groups or communities that face barriers to having their experiences and needs reflected in local services and decisions.
  • Barriers affecting those groups and measures that could support their meaningful participation in local decision-making.
  • What would make a city a Human Rights City and what concrete action local authorities or other responsible actors should take.

The survey also asks about young people’s involvement in municipal decision-making, including whether formal youth engagement mechanisms exist, whether youth recommendations influence decisions, and whether young people’s needs and rights are considered in municipal planning, budgeting, and service delivery.

Which Groups and Issues Does the Survey Consider?

The survey asks respondents to identify, where relevant, communities that may face barriers to participation or representation. These include young people, women, persons with disabilities, migrants or refugees, LGBTIQ+ persons, Indigenous Peoples, racial, ethnic or linguistic minorities, religious minorities, persons in conflict with the law, people experiencing socioeconomic disadvantage, older persons, children, and people experiencing homelessness.

Participants may select up to five groups and describe the barriers they face. The survey also asks what measures could make local decision-making more inclusive, considering accessibility, information, representation, consultation, and support.

Survey Duration and Privacy

The survey is expected to take approximately 5 to 15 minutes, depending on how many questions a participant chooses to answer. Questions marked with an asterisk are required.

The survey is anonymous. Responses will not be published in full. By submitting a response, participants agree that summaries of their contributions, together with those of other participants, may be used in analyses, reports, and public materials.

The form does not automatically collect information such as a participant’s name or email address unless they choose to provide it. Participants are asked to avoid including personal or identifying details in their answers.

Important: The survey organizers specifically ask participants not to use AI to respond. They want to hear each participant’s own views and experiences, expressed in their own words. Anyone completing the survey should therefore prepare their answers independently rather than using AI-generated responses.

Application and Participation Deadline

The Global Youth Network is an ongoing engagement platform, and the information provided does not state a deadline for joining it.

The Youth Perspectives on Human Rights Cities survey must be completed by 3 December 2026, at 23:59 Central European Time/Geneva time.

The related UN Youth Townhall session, “Human Rights Cities: From Awareness to Local Action,” is scheduled to take place in Heidelberg, Germany, from 8 to 10 December 2026.

How to Join the Network and Participate

Young people interested in joining the Global Youth Network for Human Rights can complete the Network’s sign-up form. Those wishing to contribute to the Human Rights Cities discussion can complete the separate survey by the stated deadline.

The Network and survey provide different ways to engage: joining the Network allows young people to receive updates and invitations to future activities, while the survey gives them an opportunity to share local experiences and recommendations for the Heidelberg session.

Join HERE

Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Youth Network for Human Rights.

Conclusion

The Global Youth Network for Human Rights offers young people worldwide an inclusive way to stay connected with OHCHR and participate in human rights discussions, regardless of prior experience or formal affiliation. Its email-based approach and flexible participation make it accessible to a broad range of young people.

The Human Rights Cities survey provides a timely opportunity to share perspectives on local governance, rights, inclusion, and youth participation ahead of the UN Youth Townhall in Heidelberg. Young people who choose to participate should reflect on their own communities, provide honest responses in their own words, and submit the survey by 3 December 2026.

Explore more global UN and Human Rights opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), in collaboration with the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, is inviting applications for an exciting online volunteer opportunity titled Digital Advocates for Justice, Survivor Protection and Ending Gender-Based Violence (GBV) in Cameroon. The initiative seeks to recruit 100 online volunteers to support a nationwide digital advocacy campaign aimed at preventing and responding to gender-based violence, promoting gender equality, protecting survivors and encouraging positive social behaviour.

This 12-week volunteer assignment offers an opportunity for individuals with an interest in social media advocacy, digital communication, public awareness, human rights, gender equality and community engagement to contribute to an important social development initiative. Selected volunteers will work remotely, dedicating approximately 1–5 hours per week to creating and sharing digital content, promoting campaign messages, engaging online audiences and supporting coordinated advocacy activities.

The assignment is hosted by UNDP and focuses on Cameroon, where gender-based violence remains a significant human rights and protection concern. Through the use of social media platforms and digital communities, the initiative aims to increase public awareness, challenge harmful gender norms, encourage positive behaviour and make information about available support services more accessible.

A total of 100 volunteer positions are available through a competitive recruitment process. Applicants with experience in social media communication, content creation, advocacy, public information or digital engagement are encouraged to apply. Individuals with a basic understanding of gender-based violence, gender equality or safeguarding principles will also have an advantage.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to university students, recent graduates, communication professionals, content creators, social media advocates and individuals passionate about ending violence against women and girls. Applicants with secondary-school education are eligible to apply, and people with disabilities and male candidates are strongly encouraged to submit applications.

About the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

The United Nations Development Programme is the United Nations’ global development network. It works in approximately 170 countries and territories, helping governments and communities address poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, strengthen institutions and build resilience for sustainable development.

UNDP supports countries by developing policies, strengthening leadership skills, building institutional capabilities and encouraging partnerships that can produce lasting development results. Its work covers a broad range of development priorities, including democratic governance, poverty reduction, crisis prevention and recovery, climate action, environmental protection and sustainable development.

In September 2015, world leaders adopted the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, establishing a global framework for ending poverty, protecting the planet and ensuring that all people can enjoy peace and prosperity. The agenda introduced the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which guide international development priorities through 2030.

UNDP works with governments, civil society organisations, development partners and communities to advance these goals. Its interventions are designed to strengthen national and local capacities, address development challenges and ensure that vulnerable populations are not left behind.

In Cameroon, UNDP has supported initiatives aimed at promoting recovery, stabilisation and development in communities affected by humanitarian crises. Its work has included support from development partners such as Japan, Germany, Sweden and the European Union.

The organisation has also committed to implementing the regional stabilisation strategy adopted in May 2018 by the States Parties of the Lake Chad Basin Commission (LCBC) and endorsed by the African Union.

This wider development and stabilisation work provides an important context for the digital advocacy initiative against gender-based violence.

About the Safe Spaces, Strong Voices Against GBV Project

The online volunteer assignment forms part of the broader Safe Spaces, Strong Voices Against Gender-Based Violence Project, an initiative designed to address gender-based violence through prevention, protection and empowerment strategies.

The project recognises that violence against women and girls is not only a personal or family issue but also a serious human rights, public health, social development and protection concern. It seeks to create environments where individuals, particularly women and girls, can speak out about violence, access support services and pursue justice without fear of stigma, discrimination or retaliation.

An important feature of the initiative is its focus on both physical and digital safe spaces.

Physical safe spaces can provide opportunities for affected individuals to access assistance, information and protection. Digital safe spaces, on the other hand, can help expand awareness, connect communities with reliable information and encourage conversations about preventing violence.

The project therefore seeks to use digital platforms to complement broader community-based interventions. By engaging online volunteers and influencers, it aims to reach more people, amplify messages and encourage communities to challenge harmful behaviours and attitudes that contribute to gender-based violence.

The initiative is being led by UNDP in collaboration with the United Nations Volunteers programme. It brings together the communication and advocacy capabilities of online volunteers and influencers to support a coordinated campaign against gender-based violence in Cameroon.

Understanding the Gender-Based Violence Challenge in Cameroon

Gender-based violence remains widespread in Cameroon, affecting women and girls disproportionately while also impacting men and boys. Despite government interventions and the efforts of development partners, many incidents remain unreported because of stigma, fear, limited awareness of available services and other social barriers.

The assignment description highlights the scale of the challenge through the following statistics:

  • Approximately one in three women experiences physical or sexual violence.
  • In 2024, more than 6,600 gender-based violence cases were recorded by the Ministry of Women’s Empowerment.
  • The health system documented more than 5,700 cases during the same year.
  • These health-system records included more than 2,200 cases of rape and approximately 3,500 cases of intimate partner violence.

These figures demonstrate the seriousness of the problem. However, the actual number of incidents is believed to be higher because many survivors do not report abuse or seek assistance.

Several factors contribute to underreporting. Survivors may fear being blamed, rejected or stigmatised by their families and communities. Others may not know where to obtain help or may lack confidence in the available support systems. Social and cultural attitudes can also discourage victims from speaking openly about their experiences.

Humanitarian crises have further increased the risks faced by vulnerable populations. Conflict in Cameroon’s North-West, South-West and Far North regions has created difficult conditions for women and girls, who may face heightened exposure to violence, exploitation and abuse.

Millions of people have been affected by these crises, and gender-based violence continues to be identified as a major protection concern.

The situation demonstrates the need for sustained public education, survivor-centred approaches, accessible information and stronger community engagement.

Why Digital Advocacy Is Important in the Fight Against Gender-Based Violence

The rapid growth of social media and digital communication in Cameroon provides an important opportunity to strengthen public awareness and encourage social change.

Platforms such as Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, WhatsApp and YouTube allow information to reach large audiences quickly. They also provide spaces where individuals can discuss social issues, share educational materials and promote campaigns.

However, the assignment description identifies an important gap: although social media use is growing, digital platforms have not been fully utilised for coordinated gender-based violence prevention.

Influencers can shape public attitudes and reach large audiences, while online volunteers can maintain engagement, share reliable information and help sustain advocacy activities. Yet these groups have not been systematically mobilised for coordinated campaigns.

The UNDP and UNV initiative seeks to address this gap by bringing volunteers and influencers together to support a nationwide digital advocacy effort.

Through this approach, online volunteers will help:

  1. Increase public awareness of gender-based violence and its consequences.
  2. Challenge harmful social norms, stereotypes and behaviours.
  3. Promote gender equality and women’s empowerment.
  4. Encourage positive masculinity and respectful relationships.
  5. Share information about survivor protection and available support services.
  6. Promote national and international campaigns against gender-based violence.
  7. Encourage constructive online conversations about prevention, accountability and justice.
  8. Strengthen community participation in ending violence against women and girls.

Digital advocacy is expected to complement wider prevention and protection interventions by making important messages more visible and accessible to different communities.

Overview of the UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity

The assignment is designed for individuals who want to use their digital communication and social media skills to support a meaningful development initiative.

The key details are as follows:

Opportunity detail Information
Assignment title Digital Advocates for Justice, Survivor Protection and Ending GBV in Cameroon
Host organisation United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
Collaborating programme United Nations Volunteers (UNV)
Assignment country Cameroon
Modality Online
Number of positions 100
Duration 12 weeks
Weekly commitment 1–5 hours
Recruitment method Competitive recruitment
Task type Social media presence
Area of expertise Communication, advocacy and public information
Required education level Secondary education
Sustainable Development Goal SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
Language requirements English or French communication skills
Advertisement end date 03/12/2026 at 00:00, as displayed in the vacancy

The assignment is entirely online, meaning volunteers can contribute remotely rather than relocating to Cameroon.

The expected duration is 12 weeks, with a relatively flexible weekly commitment of between one and five hours. This makes the opportunity suitable for individuals who want to contribute to a development initiative while managing their studies, employment or other responsibilities.

The recruitment process is competitive, and applicants should demonstrate that they possess the communication abilities, digital skills and commitment required to support the campaign.

Roles and Responsibilities of Selected Online Volunteers

Selected volunteers will support a nationwide digital advocacy initiative aimed at preventing and responding to gender-based violence in Cameroon.

Working remotely under the coordination of UNDP and UNV Cameroon, volunteers will contribute to public education, social media engagement, campaign promotion and the production of digital communication materials.

Their responsibilities will include the following:

1. Develop and disseminate evidence-based digital content

Volunteers will help develop and share digital materials that communicate accurate and relevant information about gender-based violence.

Content will focus on subjects such as:

  • Prevention of gender-based violence.
  • Gender equality and equal opportunities.
  • Women’s empowerment.
  • Positive masculinity.
  • Survivor protection.
  • Respectful relationships and positive social behaviour.
  • Awareness of available support services.

The emphasis will be on evidence-based information that can educate audiences and encourage constructive attitudes towards preventing violence.

Volunteers should ensure that the materials they share are responsible, respectful and appropriate for the audiences they seek to reach.

2. Share campaign materials across social media platforms

A major responsibility will involve distributing approved campaign materials across different digital platforms.

These may include:

  • Facebook
  • X (formerly Twitter)
  • Instagram
  • LinkedIn
  • TikTok
  • WhatsApp
  • YouTube

Each platform provides different opportunities for reaching audiences. For example, short videos and visual stories may be suitable for Instagram and TikTok, while longer educational posts and professional discussions may be appropriate for LinkedIn and Facebook.

Volunteers will help ensure that campaign messages reach diverse audiences through consistent and coordinated sharing.

3. Promote national and international campaigns against GBV

Volunteers will support the promotion of important national and international campaigns related to gender-based violence.

One major campaign specifically identified in the assignment description is the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence.

The 16 Days of Activism is an international campaign that raises awareness, encourages action and promotes efforts to end violence against women and girls.

Volunteers will help increase the visibility of such campaigns by sharing approved messages, digital materials and relevant information through their social media networks.

4. Participate in coordinated online advocacy campaigns

Volunteers will participate in organised digital advocacy activities using campaign messages and hashtags approved by the coordinating team.

This means that volunteers will not simply publish unrelated individual posts. They will contribute to a coordinated campaign in which participants share consistent messages to strengthen the overall visibility and impact of the initiative.

The use of approved hashtags and communication materials will help audiences identify campaign content and follow discussions across different platforms.

5. Engage respectfully with online audiences

Digital advocacy involves more than publishing information. It also requires meaningful interaction with audiences.

Volunteers will be expected to engage respectfully with people who respond to campaign materials, ask questions or participate in discussions.

Their responsibilities will include:

  • Responding appropriately to comments.
  • Encouraging constructive conversations.
  • Sharing verified information.
  • Directing individuals to reliable information and available support services where appropriate.
  • Promoting respectful discussions about gender equality and violence prevention.

Because gender-based violence is a sensitive subject, volunteers must communicate carefully and avoid language that could blame, shame or further harm survivors.

6. Produce creative digital communication materials

Volunteers will contribute to the development of creative digital products that make campaign messages accessible and engaging.

These materials may include:

  • Infographics.
  • Short educational videos.
  • Blogs and articles.
  • Survivor testimonies, where appropriately approved and handled.
  • Podcasts.
  • Animations.
  • Visual stories.
  • Social media posts and graphics.

Different formats can help communicate information to different audiences. Infographics, for example, can simplify statistics and key messages, while short videos can make educational content more engaging.

All materials should support the objectives of the campaign and follow appropriate ethical and communication standards.

7. Support behaviour change communication

Another important responsibility is to support communication activities that challenge harmful gender norms and stereotypes.

Gender-based violence is often reinforced by attitudes and beliefs that normalise discrimination, unequal power relationships, intimidation or violence.

Volunteers will help promote messages that encourage equality, mutual respect, accountability and positive masculinity.

The aim is to contribute to a gradual change in attitudes and behaviours that can help prevent violence and create safer communities.

8. Monitor social media trends and provide feedback

Volunteers will monitor relevant social media conversations and emerging trends relating to gender-based violence.

This will help the coordinating team understand what audiences are discussing, identify emerging issues and assess how campaign messages are being received.

Volunteers will provide regular feedback on audience engagement and relevant developments observed across digital platforms.

Such information can help strengthen future communication strategies and improve the effectiveness of the campaign.

9. Collaborate with other Online UN Volunteers

The initiative will involve 100 online volunteer positions, making teamwork and coordination important elements of the assignment.

Volunteers will collaborate with other participants to increase campaign visibility, share information and amplify advocacy messages.

Working collectively will help create a broader digital network capable of reaching different audiences and sustaining public engagement throughout the assignment.

10. Participate in virtual orientation and capacity-building activities

Volunteers will be expected to participate in virtual orientation sessions, capacity-building workshops and periodic coordination meetings.

These activities will help participants understand the objectives of the initiative, the campaign’s communication approach and the expectations associated with their volunteer responsibilities.

They will also provide opportunities for volunteers to exchange ideas, improve their advocacy skills and coordinate their activities.

11. Submit monthly activity reports

Volunteers will submit brief monthly reports documenting their online activities, audience engagement and campaign achievements.

These reports will help the coordinating team understand the contributions made by participants and assess the progress of the digital advocacy initiative.

Reporting may cover the digital content shared, campaign activities supported, audience interactions and other relevant achievements.

Expected Results and Impact of the Assignment

By the end of the 12-week assignment, the Online UN Volunteers are expected to have contributed to several important results.

These results are connected to the broader objective of increasing awareness, strengthening digital advocacy and encouraging action against gender-based violence.

1. Increased public awareness of gender-based violence

One expected result is improved public understanding of gender-based violence, its causes, consequences and prevention.

Through digital content and social media engagement, volunteers will help make important information available to wider audiences.

This may encourage individuals and communities to recognise harmful behaviours, understand the rights of survivors and become more aware of available support services.

2. Expanded digital reach and engagement

The campaign seeks to increase the visibility of GBV prevention messages across social media platforms.

By coordinating the efforts of 100 online volunteers and influencers, the initiative aims to reach broader audiences and encourage more people to participate in conversations about preventing violence.

3. Production of high-quality digital content

Volunteers are expected to contribute to the production and dissemination of useful digital materials, including infographics, short videos, articles, podcasts, animations and visual stories.

These resources will support the communication objectives of the campaign and provide audiences with accessible educational information.

4. Support for national and international campaigns

Volunteers will help strengthen the visibility of campaigns against gender-based violence, including the 16 Days of Activism.

Their participation will contribute to coordinated advocacy activities and encourage broader public engagement with national and international efforts to end violence.

5. Promotion of positive behaviour change

The initiative aims to challenge harmful stereotypes and promote positive social attitudes.

Through educational communication, volunteers will help encourage gender equality, women’s empowerment, positive masculinity and respectful relationships.

6. Stronger online community engagement

The campaign also seeks to strengthen interaction between digital communities and individuals interested in preventing gender-based violence.

By encouraging constructive discussions and sharing verified information, volunteers will contribute to online spaces where people can learn, exchange ideas and engage with the issue responsibly.

Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements

The UNDP online volunteer assignment is open to applicants who meet the minimum education requirements and can demonstrate an interest or experience in digital communication, social media advocacy or public engagement.

Unlike some international volunteer opportunities that require a university degree, this assignment identifies secondary or high-school completion as the minimum educational requirement.

University students, recent graduates and individuals with diplomas or degrees in relevant disciplines are strongly encouraged to apply.

Applicants should pay attention to the following requirements.

1. Educational qualifications

Applicants must have completed secondary or high-school education.

Although a university degree is not compulsory, students and graduates from relevant academic backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply.

Relevant fields of study include:

  • Communication.
  • Journalism.
  • Social Sciences.
  • Gender Studies.
  • Law.
  • Public Health.
  • Education.
  • Psychology.
  • International Relations.
  • Development Studies.
  • Information Technology.
  • Marketing.
  • Multimedia.
  • Other related disciplines.

The diversity of these fields reflects the interdisciplinary nature of the assignment. Gender-based violence involves issues relating to human rights, public health, law, education, social behaviour and development. Applicants from different academic backgrounds can therefore contribute valuable perspectives.

2. Experience in social media and digital advocacy

Applicants should demonstrate experience using social media platforms for communication, advocacy, awareness raising or public engagement.

Experience may include managing social media pages, creating awareness campaigns, sharing educational materials, promoting community initiatives or participating in online advocacy activities.

Applicants should also demonstrate the ability to create engaging digital content, including:

  • Graphics.
  • Short videos.
  • Blog posts.
  • Articles.
  • Social media captions.
  • Other digital communication materials.

Professional experience is useful, but applicants should clearly demonstrate any relevant practical experience they have gained through volunteering, academic activities, personal projects or community initiatives.

3. Understanding of gender-based violence and gender equality

A basic understanding of gender-based violence, gender equality or safeguarding principles is an advantage.

Applicants should ideally understand why gender-based violence is a serious social and human rights issue and why communication about survivors must be handled with sensitivity.

Knowledge of gender equality, women’s empowerment, survivor protection and violence prevention can help volunteers produce more responsible and meaningful campaign content.

However, the assignment does not state that advanced professional expertise in gender-based violence is compulsory.

4. Strong writing and communication skills

Good writing and communication skills are important because volunteers will be expected to develop, share and promote campaign messages.

Applicants should be able to communicate information clearly, write engaging social media content and interact respectfully with different audiences.

The assignment accepts communication skills in English and/or French.

5. Commitment to ethical online communication

Because the campaign addresses sensitive issues, volunteers must demonstrate a commitment to respectful and ethical online communication.

This includes treating survivors with dignity, avoiding harmful stereotypes, sharing verified information and engaging with audiences responsibly.

Applicants should understand the importance of protecting individual dignity and avoiding content that could expose survivors to stigma, discrimination or further harm.

6. Knowledge of digital communication tools

Familiarity with digital content creation and social media management tools is an advantage.

The assignment specifically identifies the following tools:

  • Canva.
  • CapCut.
  • Adobe Express.
  • Meta Business Suite.
  • Hootsuite.
  • Similar digital communication platforms.

These tools can help volunteers design graphics, edit videos, schedule content and manage online engagement.

However, knowledge of these tools is not mandatory. Applicants can still be considered if they possess the required communication abilities and relevant social media experience.

Language Requirements

Cameroon is a bilingual country where French and English are the main languages.

The assignment requires applicants to have proficiency and strong writing skills in English and/or French.

The language information provided in the vacancy identifies both French and English at working knowledge level as desirable.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in at least one of the two languages and produce content suitable for the audiences they are expected to reach.

Knowledge of both languages can be an advantage because it may help volunteers communicate campaign messages across different linguistic communities in Cameroon.

Key Competencies and Personal Attributes

In addition to educational qualifications and digital communication experience, successful volunteers are expected to demonstrate several professional and personal competencies.

These include:

1. Integrity and professionalism

Volunteers should act honestly, responsibly and professionally when carrying out their assignments.

They must communicate accurately, respect the objectives of the initiative and follow the standards expected of individuals supporting a United Nations programme.

2. Respect for diversity and inclusion

The campaign requires volunteers who respect people from different backgrounds and understand the importance of inclusive communication.

This is particularly important when addressing gender, violence, disability and other sensitive social issues.

3. Accountability and responsibility

Volunteers should take responsibility for their assigned tasks, meet agreed expectations and provide accurate reports of their activities.

4. Teamwork and collaboration

The assignment involves collaboration with other online volunteers and coordination with the UNDP and UNV teams.

Applicants should be comfortable working with others, sharing ideas and contributing to collective objectives.

5. Planning and organisation

Volunteers should be able to organise their activities, manage their time and contribute consistently throughout the 12-week assignment.

6. Effective communication

Clear communication is essential for creating digital content, sharing information and engaging with online audiences.

7. Creativity and innovation

The assignment requires individuals who can develop engaging ways to communicate important messages.

Creative thinking can help make complex topics easier to understand and encourage more people to engage with the campaign.

8. Adaptability and flexibility

Social media trends and online discussions can change quickly. Volunteers should be able to adapt their communication approaches while remaining consistent with approved campaign messages.

9. Results orientation

Applicants should be motivated by the results of their work and understand how their activities contribute to the wider objectives of the initiative.

10. Digital communication and online advocacy

Volunteers should understand how digital platforms can be used to share information, promote social causes and encourage constructive public engagement.

11. Content creation and storytelling

The ability to communicate important issues through stories, articles, graphics and videos will be valuable throughout the assignment.

12. Basic graphic design and multimedia production

Although not compulsory, basic skills in graphic design, video editing and multimedia production are desirable.

13. Digital literacy

Applicants should be comfortable using online platforms and digital tools to complete their assigned activities.

14. Online community engagement

Volunteers should be able to interact respectfully with audiences, encourage constructive discussions and promote responsible participation.

15. Information sharing and knowledge management

The assignment requires participants to share reliable information and contribute to the organisation of campaign knowledge and communication materials.

16. Ethical online conduct and digital safety

Volunteers must understand the importance of protecting privacy, sharing information responsibly and avoiding harmful digital behaviour.

17. Passion for gender equality and ending violence against women and girls

A genuine commitment to gender equality and the prevention of violence is central to the assignment.

18. Initiative and self-motivation

Because the opportunity is conducted online and requires independent contributions, volunteers should be proactive and capable of managing their responsibilities.

19. Commitment to volunteerism and community service

Applicants should demonstrate a willingness to contribute their time and skills towards the public good.

Who Should Apply for This UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity?

This assignment is particularly suitable for people who want to use digital communication to contribute to social change.

The following groups may find the opportunity relevant:

University students: Students studying communication, journalism, law, gender studies, public health, social sciences, international relations and other relevant subjects can gain practical experience in digital advocacy.

Recent graduates: Graduates interested in development work, public information, communications and human rights can use the assignment to strengthen their experience.

Social media managers and content creators: Individuals who understand how to develop engaging digital content and manage online communities can contribute their practical skills.

Communication and journalism professionals: People with experience in public communication, media engagement, writing and storytelling can support the campaign’s educational objectives.

Human rights and gender equality advocates: Individuals interested in women’s rights, survivor protection, gender equality and violence prevention can contribute to an important public awareness initiative.

Volunteers and community organisers: People with experience supporting community projects, public education campaigns and social development activities can bring valuable perspectives to the assignment.

The vacancy also specifically encourages male candidates and persons with disabilities (PWDs) to apply.

Sustainable Development Goal Supported by the Assignment

The assignment contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

SDG 16 seeks to promote peaceful and inclusive societies, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions.

Gender-based violence is closely connected to the objectives of this goal because violence, exploitation and discrimination undermine human rights, personal security and access to justice.

By supporting digital advocacy, public education and survivor protection, the initiative contributes to efforts to create safer communities and strengthen awareness of justice and protection mechanisms.

The assignment also supports broader development priorities relating to gender equality, women’s empowerment and inclusive participation.

Volunteerism and Compensation

The opportunity is an online volunteer assignment under the United Nations Volunteers programme.

The vacancy describes volunteerism as a broad range of activities undertaken voluntarily for the general public good, where monetary reward is not the principal motivation.

Applicants should therefore understand that this is a volunteer assignment rather than a salaried employment position.

The assignment offers an opportunity to contribute professional and personal skills towards a public-interest initiative while gaining practical experience in digital communication, advocacy, teamwork and international development.

The vacancy does not specify a salary or monetary stipend.

Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity

The United Nations Volunteers programme is committed to equal opportunity and welcomes applications from qualified individuals.

The programme emphasises diversity and inclusion and expects volunteers to respect human rights and individual dignity.

As part of their commitment to UNV values, volunteers are expected to combat discrimination and respect people regardless of:

  • Race.
  • Sex.
  • Gender identity.
  • Religion.
  • Nationality.
  • Ethnic origin.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Disability.
  • Pregnancy.
  • Age.
  • Language.
  • Social origin.
  • Other personal status.

The initiative also explicitly encourages male candidates and persons with disabilities to apply.

This inclusive approach reflects the importance of ensuring that efforts to end gender-based violence involve people from different backgrounds and communities.

Application Deadline and Important Dates

Interested applicants should pay close attention to the closing date displayed in the vacancy announcement.

Advertisement end date: 3 December 2026 at 00:00, as displayed in the original listing as 03/12/2026 00:00.

Applicants should verify the date and time displayed in the official application portal before submitting their applications, particularly because the vacancy listing presents the date in numerical format.

The assignment has an expected duration of 12 weeks. However, the expected start date field in the vacancy is displayed as “Invalid Date”. Applicants should therefore consult the official vacancy information or the coordinating team for clarification about the commencement date.

How to Apply for the UNDP Online Volunteer Assignment

Interested and qualified individuals should submit their applications through the official United Nations Volunteers online volunteering platform.

The recruitment process is competitive, and applicants should ensure that their profiles and application information demonstrate their suitability for the assignment.

The following steps can help prospective applicants prepare:

Step 1: Review the assignment requirements

Carefully read the vacancy description and confirm that you meet the minimum educational requirement and can demonstrate relevant social media, communication or advocacy experience.

Pay particular attention to the required language abilities, weekly time commitment and responsibilities.

Step 2: Prepare your UNV profile

Applicants should ensure that their UNV profile contains accurate and up-to-date information about their education, professional experience, volunteering activities and relevant skills.

Highlight any experience involving:

  • Social media management.
  • Digital communication.
  • Content creation.
  • Graphic design.
  • Video editing.
  • Public awareness campaigns.
  • Human rights advocacy.
  • Gender equality initiatives.
  • Community engagement.
  • Journalism and writing.

Applicants without formal professional experience may still demonstrate relevant abilities through university projects, personal content creation, student organisations and previous volunteer activities.

Step 3: Highlight relevant digital skills

Because the assignment focuses on social media advocacy, applicants should clearly explain their ability to create and share engaging digital content.

Where applicable, mention experience using Canva, CapCut, Adobe Express, Meta Business Suite, Hootsuite or similar tools.

Applicants should also highlight their familiarity with platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, WhatsApp, YouTube and X.

Step 4: Demonstrate your understanding of the assignment

Applicants should show an understanding of the importance of preventing gender-based violence, promoting gender equality and protecting survivors.

They should demonstrate that they can communicate sensitive subjects responsibly and contribute to constructive online discussions.

Step 5: Submit your application before the deadline

Complete the application process through the official UNV platform and ensure that all required information is provided before the advertised closing date.

Applicants are encouraged to submit early rather than wait until the final hours.

Click HERE for more information

Important Information About the Recruitment Process

Applicants should keep the following points in mind:

  • There are 100 online volunteer assignments available.
  • Recruitment is competitive; meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection.
  • The assignment lasts 12 weeks.
  • Volunteers are expected to contribute approximately 1–5 hours per week.
  • The assignment is conducted online.
  • The minimum educational requirement is secondary or high-school completion.
  • University students and graduates from relevant fields are strongly encouraged to apply.
  • Experience in social media advocacy and digital content creation is important.
  • English and/or French communication skills are required.
  • Knowledge of Canva, CapCut, Adobe Express, Meta Business Suite or Hootsuite is an advantage but is not compulsory.
  • Male candidates and persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.
  • The vacancy does not specify a salary or stipend.

Beware of Recruitment Scams

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fees in connection with its recruitment process.

Applicants should never pay money to an individual or organisation claiming to guarantee selection or facilitate recruitment into this volunteer assignment.

They should also exercise caution when sharing personal information online. UN emblems, logos, names and addresses can be copied or reproduced by fraudulent individuals and organisations.

Applications should only be submitted through the official United Nations Volunteers recruitment platform.

Conclusion

The UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity for Digital Advocates for Justice, Survivor Protection and Ending Gender-Based Violence in Cameroon offers an important opportunity for individuals to use their communication and digital skills to support a meaningful social development initiative.

With 100 online volunteer positions, a 12-week duration and a weekly commitment of just 1–5 hours, the assignment provides an accessible way for students, graduates, content creators, communication professionals and social advocates to contribute to a nationwide campaign against gender-based violence.

Through social media content creation, public awareness campaigns, online engagement and collaboration with other volunteers, participants will help promote gender equality, challenge harmful social norms, increase awareness of survivor protection and encourage positive behaviour.

The initiative also provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in digital advocacy, public communication, content creation and international development while contributing to the United Nations’ broader development objectives.

Applicants do not need a university degree to qualify, as secondary education is the minimum requirement. However, relevant experience in social media communication, advocacy, writing or digital content creation will be valuable. Individuals with disabilities and male candidates are particularly encouraged to apply.

Interested applicants should review the requirements carefully and submit their applications through the official UNV platform before the advertised closing date.

Application deadline: 3 December 2026 at 00:00, as displayed in the vacancy announcement.

item.content:encoded:
Introduction

Are you an experienced professional in sport, sports agencies, brands, digital media or technology who wants to help make childhood safer and more fulfilling? UNICEF UK is inviting applications for three new members to join its Sport Advisory Board, offering an opportunity to contribute expertise and professional networks to work that supports children’s rights.

The UNICEF UK Sport Advisory Board was established in 2022 to connect knowledge and networks from across the sports sector with UNICEF UK’s work for children. Board members provide advice, make connections and offer practical support to help UNICEF UK build relationships across sport, identify fundraising opportunities and advance children’s rights.

The role is voluntary and unpaid, with an estimated commitment of two to three hours per month. Applications close at 9:00 a.m. on Monday, 30 November 2026.

About the UNICEF UK Sport Advisory Board

Sport has the power to inspire people, bring communities together and reach audiences around the world. UNICEF UK uses the reach of sport to raise funds, champion children’s rights and help make sport safer for children.

The Sport Advisory Board brings together people with relevant expertise and networks to support this work. It was established in 2022 and currently has six members. UNICEF UK is seeking three additional members to expand the board’s experience and connections.

Board members contribute advice and practical support in areas such as:

  • Building relationships across the sports sector
  • Identifying potential fundraising opportunities
  • Connecting UNICEF UK with relevant organisations and networks
  • Supporting efforts to advance children’s rights
  • Helping strengthen the connection between sport and UNICEF UK’s work for children

The role is suited to people who can contribute professional insight, relationships and practical ideas. Applicants do not need to have previous experience working for a charity or UNICEF to express their interest.

Who UNICEF UK Is Looking For

UNICEF UK welcomes motivated applicants from across sport, with particular interest in people who have experience in:

Sports agencies

Professionals from sports agencies may bring knowledge of the sports industry, relationships with athletes or organisations, and an understanding of how sport partnerships are developed.

Brands

Applicants with brand-related experience may contribute insight into partnerships, audience engagement and opportunities to connect organisations in support of children’s rights.

Digital and technology

People working in digital and technology may offer expertise in digital platforms, innovation, technology-enabled engagement or other relevant areas that can support UNICEF UK’s work.

These are areas of particular interest rather than an exhaustive list of acceptable backgrounds. UNICEF UK states that relevant experience can come from many settings. Applicants do not need to have worked for UNICEF or in the charity sector to apply.

Responsibilities and Contribution

Sport Advisory Board members provide advice, connections and practical support to UNICEF UK. Their contribution is focused on helping the organisation make effective use of the sports sector’s reach and expertise.

The board’s work includes supporting relationship-building across sport, identifying fundraising opportunities and helping advance children’s rights. Members may use their professional experience and networks to offer relevant perspectives, make connections and support UNICEF UK’s efforts to make sport safer for children.

The role is advisory and voluntary. It is not described as a paid staff position.

Time Commitment and Working Arrangements

The role requires approximately two to three hours per month, including a quarterly board meeting.

Meetings are usually held during working hours and may take place either at UNICEF UK’s London office or online. The role is therefore described as part home-based and part office-based, with London as the listed location.

Applicants should consider whether they can make the monthly time commitment and attend quarterly meetings, including meetings scheduled during the working day.

Is the UNICEF UK Sport Advisory Board Member Role Paid?

No. This is a voluntary, unpaid role. It does not offer a salary.

The time commitment is estimated at two to three hours per month, including quarterly board meetings. Applicants should take these arrangements into account when deciding whether the opportunity fits their availability and circumstances.

Application Requirements and Important Guidance

Applicants are expected to demonstrate their knowledge, skills and understanding of the role requirements, as well as how UNICEF UK’s values and mission align with their own.

Before applying, candidates should review the role’s job description, which outlines the criteria they will need to address in their application. They should also read UNICEF UK’s organisational values, referred to as its “Our Shared Commitment.”

The recruitment information also provides details about UNICEF UK’s benefits, fair and inclusive recruitment approach, and application support. Although the board role itself is voluntary and unpaid, applicants can review these organisational resources to understand UNICEF UK’s recruitment approach and candidate support.

Important notice about the use of AI

UNICEF UK explicitly states that using artificial intelligence tools, including ChatGPT, to generate answers to its application questions will automatically exclude an application from the recruitment process.

Applicants should therefore prepare their application answers themselves, ensuring that they accurately reflect their own experience, knowledge, skills and understanding of the role. They should carefully follow the instructions provided by UNICEF UK.

Application Deadline and Recruitment Timeline

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

Recruitment stage Date
Application deadline 9:00 a.m., Monday, 30 November 2026
First interview date Friday, 18 December 2026

The application deadline is stated as 9:00 a.m., not the end of the day. Candidates should submit their applications before that time and allow sufficient time to complete all required sections.

Click HERE for more information about UNICEF UK Sport Advisory Board Member 2026.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should review the Sport Advisory Board Member job description and the application requirements before submitting their application through UNICEF UK’s recruitment process.

The job description contains the criteria candidates will need to respond to. Applicants should also review UNICEF UK’s organisational values and ensure that their application explains, in their own words, how their knowledge, skills and experience relate to the role.

The opportunity is for three new board members. Candidates should submit their applications by 9:00 a.m. on Monday, 30 November 2026.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The UNICEF UK Sport Advisory Board Member opportunity is intended for motivated professionals who can contribute expertise, networks and practical advice to support children’s rights through sport. With particular interest in people from sports agencies, brands, digital and technology, the board offers a way to connect professional experience with UNICEF UK’s work to raise funds, champion children’s rights and help make sport safer for children.

The role is voluntary and unpaid, requires approximately two to three hours per month, and includes quarterly meetings held in London or online. Interested candidates should review the role criteria and application guidance carefully, especially UNICEF UK’s explicit rule against using AI to generate application answers.

Applications must be submitted by 9:00 a.m. on Monday, 30 November 2026. The first interview is scheduled for Friday, 18 December 2026.

Discover more global Volunteer Opportunities on Opportunities For Youth.

item.content:encoded:
TikTok is inviting applications from young people around the world to join its TikTok Youth Council 2026–27, an international youth participation initiative that gives teenagers an opportunity to share their perspectives and contribute to discussions about online safety, digital experiences, platform policies, and product development.

The TikTok Youth Council brings together young people from different countries, cultures, and backgrounds to help TikTok better understand the experiences, concerns, and needs of teenagers using its platform. Selected members will have the opportunity to work with other young people internationally and engage directly with TikTok’s policy and product teams.

The initiative is particularly suitable for teenagers who are passionate about youth advocacy, interested in online safety and digital issues, and motivated to make a positive contribution to the online experiences of young people.

Applications are currently open for the 2027 council, with eligible applicants required to submit their applications by 14 December 2026.

1. Overview of the TikTok Youth Council 2026–27

The TikTok Youth Council is an international youth engagement initiative led by Praesidio Safeguarding on behalf of TikTok.

Through this initiative, TikTok aims to involve teenagers in conversations and decision-making processes concerning the platform’s policies, products, and approaches to supporting young users.

The council provides a space where young people can express their opinions, discuss challenges affecting teenagers online, exchange ideas, and provide feedback to the teams responsible for developing and improving TikTok.

Members will work collaboratively with other selected teenagers from different global regions. Their contributions will help inform TikTok’s understanding of young people’s experiences and perspectives.

The 2027 council will operate between January and December 2027, requiring members to participate in a series of virtual meetings and maintain ongoing engagement throughout the year.

2. Objectives of the TikTok Youth Council

The TikTok Youth Council is designed to ensure that young people’s perspectives are considered when discussing the digital environments they use.

Its main objectives include:

  • Amplifying young people’s voices: Providing teenagers with an opportunity to communicate their experiences, concerns, opinions, and recommendations directly to TikTok.
  • Improving online experiences: Helping TikTok understand the challenges teenagers encounter while using social media and digital platforms.
  • Informing platform policies: Allowing young people to contribute perspectives that can help inform TikTok’s policies and approaches to youth-related issues.
  • Supporting product development: Giving council members an opportunity to share feedback with TikTok’s product teams about features and experiences that affect young users.
  • Encouraging international collaboration: Bringing together teenagers from different countries and backgrounds to exchange ideas and learn from one another.
  • Promoting respectful discussions: Creating an inclusive environment where young people can discuss difficult topics, listen to different viewpoints, and contribute constructively.

The initiative recognises that teenagers have valuable firsthand knowledge of their online experiences and that their perspectives can contribute to improving digital platforms.

3. What Will Selected Youth Council Members Do?

Selected members will participate in a series of activities throughout the council period, which runs from January to December 2027.

Their responsibilities will involve more than simply attending occasional meetings. Applicants should be prepared to make an ongoing commitment and actively contribute to the council’s discussions and collaborative activities.

Expected responsibilities include:

Participating in Virtual Meetings

Council members will attend a series of virtual meetings scheduled throughout 2027. These meetings will provide opportunities to discuss different topics affecting teenagers online and exchange perspectives with other members.

Since the council brings together young people from different global regions, participants should be comfortable communicating in English.

Sharing Opinions and Experiences

Members will be expected to share their views, experiences, and ideas concerning issues that affect teenagers in digital spaces.

They should be willing to discuss topics in depth, explain their perspectives, and contribute constructive suggestions.

Working with International Participants

The council will bring together teenagers from a range of cultural, geographical, and social backgrounds.

Members will need to collaborate respectfully with other participants, appreciate different viewpoints, and contribute positively to group discussions.

Completing Additional Reading and Preparation

Participation will also involve additional reading and preparation outside scheduled meetings.

Members should be prepared to review relevant materials, explore discussion topics, and complete preparatory reading before meetings.

Collaborating Outside Scheduled Meetings

There will be ongoing collaboration between council members beyond the formal virtual meetings.

Applicants should therefore be able to dedicate sufficient time to communication, preparation, and other council-related activities throughout the year.

4. Eligibility Criteria for the TikTok Youth Council 2026–27

The opportunity is open to teenagers who meet the age, communication, participation, and engagement requirements.

Applicants must satisfy the following eligibility conditions:

Age Requirements

  • Applicants must be at least 14 years old at the beginning of the council in January 2027.
  • Applicants must not be older than 19 by the end of December 2027.
  • The opportunity is particularly aimed at young people aged 14–18.

TikTok Usage

Applicants should be TikTok users who understand the platform and have an interest in issues affecting young people online.

Youth Advocacy

Candidates should be passionate about youth advocacy and interested in contributing to discussions that could improve online experiences for teenagers.

English Language Requirements

All applicants must have a good understanding of English and be able to communicate in English during virtual meetings.

Communication and Collaboration Skills

Applicants should demonstrate the ability to:

  • Communicate their opinions and ideas clearly.
  • Listen respectfully to different perspectives.
  • Work constructively with other young people.
  • Participate in discussions involving individuals from different backgrounds.
  • Discuss topics and issues affecting teenagers online.
  • Share ideas in a supportive and respectful environment.
  • Demonstrate curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Availability and Commitment

Applicants must be able to commit to a series of virtual meetings between January and December 2027.

They should also be willing to participate in ongoing collaboration outside scheduled meetings and complete additional reading in preparation for discussions.

Parental or Carer Permission

Applicants will need permission from a parent or carer to apply.

5. Who Is Encouraged to Apply?

TikTok and Praesidio Safeguarding are particularly interested in creating an inclusive, welcoming, and supportive council that represents young people from different backgrounds and circumstances.

Applications are especially encouraged from teenagers belonging to underrepresented or marginalised communities, including:

  • Young people from ethnic minority communities.
  • Young people from religious minority communities.
  • LGBTQ+ individuals.
  • Young people living with disabilities.
  • Refugees and migrants.
  • Young people currently living in foster care.
  • Individuals who are experiencing or have previously experienced homelessness.

These groups are specifically highlighted in the application announcement as communities whose participation is particularly welcome.

However, the opportunity is not exclusively restricted to these groups. Other teenagers who meet the eligibility requirements and demonstrate an interest in youth advocacy and online issues are also encouraged to apply.

The initiative aims to create a diverse council where participants can bring different experiences, ideas, and perspectives to discussions.

6. Geographic Eligibility: Who Can Apply?

The TikTok Youth Council is described as an international initiative that brings together young people from different countries and global regions.

The announcement does not publish a specific list of eligible countries or impose a particular nationality requirement.

It therefore presents the opportunity as internationally oriented rather than restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent.

Young people from different geographical regions may consider applying, provided they satisfy the age, English-language, TikTok usage, and participation requirements.

However, applicants should check the official application form for any additional country-specific conditions or restrictions before submitting their applications.

7. Duration and Participation Format

The TikTok Youth Council 2026–27 will operate for approximately one year.

Important programme details include:

  • Programme period: January to December 2027.
  • Participation format: Virtual meetings.
  • Meeting frequency: A series of meetings throughout the year; the exact schedule is not specified in the announcement.
  • Additional activities: Ongoing collaboration between council members outside scheduled meetings.
  • Preparation: Additional reading and preparation before meetings.
  • Working language: English.

Because the programme involves activities throughout the year, applicants should carefully consider their availability before applying.

Teenagers who have school commitments or other responsibilities should ensure they can manage the expected participation alongside their existing schedules.

8. Benefits of Joining the TikTok Youth Council

Becoming a member of the TikTok Youth Council offers an opportunity to participate in international youth advocacy and contribute to discussions about one of the world’s major social media platforms.

Some of the key potential benefits include:

Opportunity to Influence TikTok Policies and Products

Members will have an opportunity to advise and inform TikTok’s policy and product teams.

Their perspectives can help the platform better understand the needs, experiences, and concerns of teenagers.

International Youth Networking

Participants will collaborate with young people from different global regions and backgrounds, creating opportunities to exchange ideas and develop international connections.

Youth Leadership and Advocacy Experience

The council provides an opportunity to strengthen youth advocacy skills by participating in discussions, sharing recommendations, and representing young people’s perspectives.

Improved Communication Skills

Regular participation in virtual meetings and collaborative discussions can help members develop their ability to communicate ideas, listen to others, and engage in constructive conversations.

Understanding Digital Safety and Online Issues

Participants will have opportunities to explore topics affecting teenagers online and engage in discussions about the digital experiences of young people.

Experience Working with International Teams

Collaborating with other young people and contributing to discussions involving TikTok’s policy and product teams can provide valuable exposure to international teamwork and consultation processes.

Important: The official announcement does not specify financial compensation, a stipend, travel funding, certificates, or other monetary benefits. Applicants should not assume that these are included.

9. Application Process: How to Apply for the TikTok Youth Council 2026–27

Interested and eligible teenagers can apply through the official online application form provided by Praesidio Safeguarding.

Follow these steps:

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements

Before applying, ensure that you meet the age requirements and can communicate effectively in English.

You should also be a TikTok user with an interest in youth advocacy and issues affecting teenagers online.

Step 2: Discuss Your Application with a Parent or Carer

Parental or carer permission is required to apply. Make sure you have the necessary permission before submitting your application.

Step 3: Prepare Your Application

Think about your experiences, opinions, interests, and reasons for wanting to join the council.

Consider how you could contribute to discussions about young people’s online experiences and collaborate with teenagers from different backgrounds.

Step 4: Complete the Online Application Form

Visit the official application form and provide the information requested.

Make sure that your answers are accurate and that you submit all required information.

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Complete and submit your application before the official closing date.

Late applications may not be considered, so applicants are encouraged to apply well before the deadline.

10. Important Dates and Application Deadline

Applicants should take note of the following deadline:

  • Application deadline: Monday, 14 December 2026.
  • Closing time: 5:00 PM GMT.
  • Programme commencement: January 2027.
  • Programme conclusion: December 2027.

Applications must be received by Monday, 14 December 2026, at 5:00 PM GMT.

Applicants should account for the time difference in their respective countries and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications.

11. Important Considerations Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should consider the following points:

  1. Age eligibility: You must meet the specified age requirements at the beginning and end of the council period.
  2. English proficiency: You must be comfortable communicating in English during virtual meetings.
  3. TikTok experience: You should have a good understanding of TikTok as a platform and an interest in its impact on young people.
  4. Time commitment: You must be available for virtual meetings and ongoing collaboration throughout 2027.
  5. Preparation requirements: You should be willing to complete additional reading outside scheduled meetings.
  6. Parental or carer permission: You must obtain permission before applying.
  7. Application deadline: Your application must be received by 14 December 2026 at 5:00 PM GMT.
  8. Country-specific requirements: Check the application form for any additional geographical eligibility conditions.

    Official Application and Further Information

    Official Application Form:
    https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=qlPR3OIEGUCsos1JGGbFNRgkYoJd4v5JhyxRgN2t_fhUQUxWR0tETTlRMTJXNlZJOE9aNVRDN0tLVCQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl

    Official Opportunity Announcement:
    https://praesidiosafeguarding.co.uk/tiktok-youth-council-2026-27/

    Organising Organisation – Praesidio Safeguarding:
    https://praesidiosafeguarding.co.uk/

    Contact Email:
    info@praesidiosafeguarding.co.uk

Conclusion

The TikTok Youth Council 2026–27 is an international youth participation opportunity for teenagers interested in digital platforms, online safety, youth advocacy, and social media policy. It provides young people with an opportunity to share their perspectives, collaborate with teenagers from different backgrounds, and contribute to discussions with TikTok’s policy and product teams.

The initiative is particularly relevant for young people who want to understand how digital platforms work, raise awareness about issues affecting teenagers online, and participate in conversations that could help improve the online experiences of young users.

Applicants aged 14–18 who meet the eligibility requirements, have a good understanding of English, and can commit to the programme throughout 2027 are encouraged to consider applying. Young people from underrepresented communities, including ethnic and religious minorities, LGBTQ+ individuals, refugees, migrants, and people living with disabilities, are particularly encouraged to participate.

Interested candidates should obtain permission from a parent or carer and complete the online application before Monday, 14 December 2026, at 5:00 PM GMT.

Apply now to become a member of the TikTok Youth Council 2026–27 and contribute your voice to conversations shaping the digital experiences of young people.

 

Explore more Volunteering at Opportunities for Youth (OFY).
